in_arabic.name: كيسوة
in_arabic.meaning: الكسوة الشرفية التي تغطي الكعبة المشرفة
in_arabic.long_meaning: الكيسوة هي الكسوة الشرفية التي تغطي الكعبة المشرفة في مكة المكرمة، وهي من الشعائر الإسلامية المهمة. تأتي الكيسوة من الجذر العربي 'ك-س-ى' والذي يعني التغطية أو الستر. تاريخياً، كانت الكيسوة تُصنع يدوياً من الحرير الأسود وتُزيّن بآيات من القرآن الكريم. للكيسوة أهمية روحية كبيرة حيث أنها تغطي الكعبة التي هي قبلة المسلمين الأولى.

in_urdu.name: کيسوا
in_urdu.long_meaning: کيسوا کا مطلب ہے کعبہ مشرف کی شرفیہ چادر جو مکہ مکرمہ میں واقع ہے۔ یہ اسلامی رسموں کا ایک اہم حصہ ہے۔ عربی جڑ 'ك-س-ى' سے نکلا ہے جس کا مطلب ہے ڈھانپنا یا چھپانا۔ تاریخی طور پر، کيسوا ہاتھ سے بنایا ہوا سیاہ ریشم کا لبادہ ہوتا تھا جس پر قرآن کی آیات درج ہوتی تھیں۔ کيسوا کی روحانی اہمیت بہت زیادہ ہے کیونکہ یہ کعبہ کو ڈھانپتا ہے جو مسلمانوں کی پہلی قبلہ ہے۔

in_hindi.name: किसवा
in_hindi.long_meaning: किसवा का अर्थ है काबा की शरीफिया चादर, जो मक्का में स्थित है। यह एक महत्वपूर्ण इस्लामी रस्म है। यह 'ك-س-ى' नामक अरबी मूल से निकला है, जिसका अर्थ है ढकना या ओढ़ना। ऐतिहासिक रूप से, किसवा हाथ से बना हुआ काला रेशम का लबादा होता था जिस पर कुरआन की आयतें लिखी होती थीं। किसवा की आध्यात्मिक महत्ता बहुत अधिक है क्योंकि यह काबा को ढकता है, जो मुसलमानों की पहली किबला है।

in_english.name: Kiswa
in_english.meaning: The sacred covering of the Kaaba
in_english.long_meaning: Kiswa refers to the sacred covering of the Kaaba in Mecca, Saudi Arabia. Etymologically derived from the Arabic root 'ك-س-ى' (k-s-y), meaning to cover or clothe. Historically, the Kiswa was a hand-made black silk cloth adorned with verses from the Quran. It holds significant spiritual importance as it covers the Kaaba, the first qibla (direction of prayer) for Muslims worldwide. The Kiswa is renewed annually on the day of Arafah during Hajj, symbolizing renewal and devotion.

data.cultural_impact: The Kiswa is not just a simple piece of clothing but a significant aspect of Islamic culture and heritage. The tradition of covering the Kaaba with Kiswa dates back to the early Islamic period and has been continued until today. The changing of the Kiswa during Hajj Pilgrimage is a grand ceremony attended by thousands of pilgrims. Each new Kiswa is intricately designed and adorned with beautiful calligraphy and geometric patterns, representing the rich artistic heritage of Islamic culture.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the Kiswa symbolizes the idea of Tawhid or the Oneness of God in Islam. The Kaaba is a symbol of the unity of God and the Kiswa represents the protective covering and presence of God in our lives. The act of covering the Kaaba with the Kiswa also highlights the importance of humility and modesty in Islam, as the holiest site in Islam is covered and protected, reminding Muslims to do the same with their own bodies and actions. Additionally, the Kiswa also symbolizes the idea of unity and solidarity among Muslims, as they come together during Hajj to participate in this important ceremony.

historical_references.reference: From the 7th century CE, the Kaaba's door was covered with a single piece of silk or brocade, called the Kiswa. The Kiswa was replaced every year during the Hajj pilgrimage.
historical_references.context: The Kaaba, Islam's holiest site, was covered with a new Kiswa every year during the annual pilgrimage.

historical_references.reference: The Kiswa, a cloth covering for the Kaaba's door, was first mentioned in historical records during the caliphate of Umar ibn Al-Khattab (634-644 CE).
historical_references.context: The Kiswa was an important part of the Kaaba's sanctity, and its first recorded mention is during the early Islamic period.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Kiswa is a large, embroidered silk or gold-brocade cloth that covers the Kaaba, the holiest site in Islam, located in Mecca, Saudi Arabia. This tradition dates back to the 7th century. In modern times, the Kiswa has gained significant popularity beyond its religious context, inspiring trends in various creative fields. The intricate designs and rich colors of the Kiswa have influenced Islamic art, with artists recreating these patterns in paintings, sculptures, and other forms. Additionally, the Kiswa's beauty and symbolism have seeped into the fashion and textiles industry, with designers featuring similar designs in their clothing lines, making it a popular choice for modern Islamic fashion. The Kiswa's influence extends to pilgrimage and spirituality as well, with people purchasing small replicas for their personal use during prayer and meditation. Social media platforms, such as Instagram, Pinterest, and Etsy, are popular spaces for showcasing and selling these replicas and inspiring designs based on the Kiswa.
